featured_reviews.name: Akshay Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Since I was living at IIT Mumbai in Powai for the next two days and my wife wanted to eat fish in Mumbai, this was the best restaurant available near IIT.

The restaurant had a nice local ambience and had a family vibe as well.

We ordered the prawn koliwada, solkadhi and if you are in Mumbai, how can you not order Bombil rawa fry.

And for dinner, I ordered a Surmai malvan thali.

Honestly, the Sol Kadhi and Bombil were outstanding.

The prawn koliwada was tad disappointing since it had a little burnt taste. May be it was over fried for a min or two extra.

But the disappointment of the evening was Surmai thali. The fish was not so fresh and was poorly marinated with less salt. The bhakri and the dry prawns salad saved the thali a bit.

I am a regular visitor to Mahesh lunch home at Saki Naka but considering the horrible traffic i faced frm Mumbai airport T1 to IIT Mumbai, i had no guts to visit mahesh lunch home.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience at Taste of Malvan in Powai, and honestly, it did not live up to the expectations of a Malvani restaurant at all. I visited on a Sunday night, and the place was almost 90% empty—which in hindsight should have been a clear sign to skip it. Unfortunately, I still decided to try it, and it turned out to be a complete mistake.

Starting with the food, the quality was extremely poor and far from authentic Malvani cuisine. Malvani food is known for its rich flavors, freshness, and bold use of spices, but what was served here felt careless and poorly prepared. The prawns butter garlic was one of the worst I have had—bland, lacking freshness, and completely disappointing. The surmai fish was another letdown; it was sliced extremely thin and did not feel like a proper serving. The taste and texture were both underwhelming.

I also ordered chicken vade, and that was equally disappointing. The vade dough clearly tasted frozen and stale. Anyone who has had fresh homemade vade can easily tell the difference—I personally can because my mom cooks vade at home, and the contrast was very obvious. What was served here lacked freshness, softness, and authenticity.

What made it worse is that the food overall did not taste fresh at all. In fact, I would say roadside food stalls serve much better and fresher Malvani food than this restaurant. That says a lot about the quality being offered here.

The only positive aspect was the service. The staff was polite, humble, and attentive, which I genuinely appreciated. However, good service alone cannot make up for such poor food quality.

Spending around ₹3500 on this meal felt like a complete waste. For that price, you expect good quality and authentic flavors, but instead, the experience was extremely disappointing.

Overall, I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for authentic Malvani cuisine or even decent seafood. There are far better options in Powai. Definitely not worth the money or the visit.

Thank you for your feedback. We’re sorry to hear that your experience did not meet expectations. Your comments on food taste and pricing are noted, and we will work on improving. We hope to serve you better on your next visit.

Warm Regards,
Team Taste of Malvan

featured_reviews.name: Yogen Sachdev
featured_reviews.review_text:
I finally revisited Maaslli – Saraswat and GSB Speciality last night for my annual catch-up with friends, and once again, it reminded me why this place is rightly awarded the best seafood restaurant in Mumbai.

We started off with their seafood soup, which was practically a treasure hunt in a bowl, packed with so many varieties of seafood that I stopped trying to count after a few spoonfuls. A rich, flavorful start that set the tone for the evening.

Next came the Bombil Fry, and let me say this: if you visit Maaslli and skip this, you’re missing the highlight of the menu. Perfectly crisp on the outside, melt-in-your-mouth inside, it was unanimously the table favorite.

The Prawns Ghee Roast, their signature dish, followed, aromatic, buttery, and spicy in all the right ways. You could taste the freshness of the prawns through the layers of ghee and masala.

I ordered the cucumber mint cooler as a palette cleanser, one of the best non-alcoholic drinks I’ve had. Truly impressed by the bar at this outlet

To round things off, we indulged in the Crab Gravy with Bhakri, a true coastal comfort combination. The gravy had that home-style depth of flavor that only comes from slow cooking and authentic spices.

Between the impeccable flavors, warm service, and the nostalgic coastal touch in every dish, Maaslli continues to set the gold standard for seafood in Mumbai. Can’t wait for next year’s reunion, though honestly, I might not wait that long to go back.

featured_reviews.name: NOSHIR KATRAK
featured_reviews.review_text:
Maaslli Restaurant & Bar, at Kemps Corner, Mumbai.
Basically a Sea food Restaurant, but also have other non veg dishes on their platter.
One cannot afford to miss the fried Bombil (Fresh, Fried Bombay Ducks).
They have a great Menu.
They do have various Thali dishes and other alcarte dishes.
It is just mouth watering and thus unable to put in words to describe the dishes.
One must enjoy the crab dishes and crab soup.
They also present you their fresh catch and you may select the fish if your choice, depending upon the weight the rate is fixed.
The atmosphere is damn cool and decent with fishes reflecting in the walls and partisans.
The curry, different types is served and we are asked to taste, then by adding coconut oil again to try. Thus if you are ordering any curry dish you can select your choice of curry.
The staff is very courteous and friendly.
The person, Mr. Anthony, accepting the order is very polite and well versed with the description of the dishes.
Service is quite fast and dishes are very tempting.
The complete crockery is if copper OR may be brass (not sure). But it is a real experience to have your food in such dish and even the fork and spoon.
The soup was something different from the normal ones which all must have experienced.
Crab soup, very tasty and hot enough and goes without saying very tasty.
Sweet dish of Modak and a sweetening dish made if milk and sprinkled with pista, woh! Lovely.
The dishes are well place and economically rated.
If you are in that area, do give a try and taste the tasty dishes, yes! Definitely one have a inclination and a taste for Sea Food.
The Bar is open and you have choices of hard drinks, Cocktails and even Mocktails.
A seperate Menu displaying the drinks is maintained.
Do visit, you will not regret nor your pockets will be pinched.
Enjoy the Sea Food and friendly service.

We ordered the paan style surmai that was wrapped in a banana leaf and roasted, the sukha bhujane prawns and the crab soup. I look forward to trying other items on their menu in the future.

featured_reviews.name: Ralph Pinto
featured_reviews.review_text:

1. Crab Lollipop: 6/10
2. Thalis with Rice Bhakaris
-a. Surmai: 10/10
-b. Pomfret: 9/10
-c. Bombil: 7/10

Crab Lollipop wasn't great. I have had better elsewhere.
It lacked the basic crab taste and the coating too was very mild on flavor.

The thalis were awesome. The fish were very fresh and tasty that it made our day. Surmai was the best. It had the best flavor, followed by Pomfret and then the Bombil. Surmai and Pomfret were rawa fry with little masala. It was just plain batter fry for the Bombil. We make better Bombil fry at home, so yeah.
The rice bhakari tasted awesome when it was hot.
Dry Prawns/Jhinga/Javla tasted good with the bhakari.
The pomfret fish and curry was very fresh and tasty.
Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Restaurant is smaller compared to the one near kemps corner. Cleanliness was decent. No washrooms. Only a basin is available. No Queue when we arrived at 8pm. But a queue started building later on.

Visited Oh! Calcutta – Tardeo, Mumbai and had a delightful dining experience overall.
Food:
Jackfruit Tikki (4/5): Nicely done with good texture and flavor, quite enjoyable.
Bhetki Fish Fry (5/5): Absolutely spot on—authentic taste and perfectly cooked, a must-try.
Hing Aloo Dum with Luchi (4/5): Very satisfying, well-balanced flavors and comforting.
Kolkata Chicken Biryani (4/5): In Mumbai, it’s rare to find good biryani. Being from Lucknow, I found the Kolkata version here to be the closest cousin to Lucknowi pulao/biryani. However, the potato lacked the signature texture of an authentic Kolkata biryani, which is why I’m deducting a point.

Service:
The staff is very helpful, especially Ashok, who made the experience smoother and more pleasant with attentive service.
Ambience & Location:
Located in the busy by-lanes of Tardeo. The place can be a bit tricky to access due to traffic, but valet service seems to be available (though I did not use it).
Overall:
A great place for authentic Bengali cuisine with a few minor misses. Definitely worth visiting for the Bhetki Fish Fry and the overall food quality.

featured_reviews.name: Danish Ansari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food Review: A Major Disappointment
​I truly believe one shouldn't speak ill of food, but I had an absolutely terrible experience here.
​We ordered the Prawns Koliwada and Crispy Chicken. Given the massive hype surrounding this restaurant, we expected the food to be exceptional. As a seafood lover—especially prawns fry—I was genuinely shocked from the very first bite. The Prawns Koliwada was completely tasteless; the spice profile was missing and there was no salt at all.
​To make matters worse, when my wife cut into a prawn, we realized they hadn't been cleaned properly. The digestive tracks (veins) were still inside. Every single prawn was like that, which completely ruined our appetite. On top of that, the dish was incredibly expensive.

​The Crispy Chicken
​The second dish was just as bad. It was so sour that after just one bite, we had to ask the waiter to pack it up. Neither my wife nor my kids could eat it—it was a total waste of money. I’ve had Crispy Chicken at many places, but this was the worst. Honestly, the local Chinese joint in my neighborhood makes it better.

​The Lesson Learned
​This experience taught me one thing: don't just rush to a restaurant based on an influencer's video. You have to check real reviews first. I have no idea what people actually like about the food there. My wife and I are beyond disappointed.

featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Keep up the good work.

I've been passing by the restaurant on the regular and always wanted to try it out. Honestly, I don't know why we didn't come here before. And now that we have, it's hand's down my favourite Sea food restaurant, in this part of town.

I really liked the whole vibe of the place, especially the hand painted murals on the 1st floor seating area. Comfortable seating, spacious yet cosy.

Their speciality being Mangalorean cuisine, we obviously had to try the staples! So we started with their superb Prawns Rava fry, coated and shallow fried in the most crunchy rava coating, is a must have. It was so good we ordered 3 plates! Same goes for their Prawns Koliwada fry, with delicious crispy bits of curry patta, adding an amazing punch of flavour! Both these come highly recommended by everyone.

You also must try their 'Sukkha Masala' - with any seafood of your choice. We went for their Teesria or clams. The masala has a heavy dose of fresh grated coconut, spices and well balanced flavors.

For the mains, Please do not leave without trying their Ghee Roast. It's the best I've had in Bombay. Right up there with the famous one from Nagarjuna, Bangalore.  Perfect roast masala with liberal amount of cashews in it. Best eaten with Neer Dosas. I just wish their quantity was a little more. It's just enough for one good eater.

The Prawn Gassi with Kori Roti is another Mangalorean speciality you cannot miss! Their Fish thalis are also very good and reasonable too.

The verdict: Superb food and good service are a delightful combination!

UPDATE: Visited the last two times and I'm sad to say that they lost the title for the best ghee roast. Since the chef changed, the dish is very mediocre, with maybe two-three bits  of cashews in it. :( Taste is not right too

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.
